# computesphere_secret_source (Resource)

Manages a secret manager connection for the account (Doppler or Azure Key Vault), which deployments and environments read secrets from, so their values never pass through Terraform. Owners and admins only. The connection is tested before it's saved: nothing is saved unless the secret manager accepts the credential. A secret manager that secrets still read from can't be removed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "doppler_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

# A Doppler config that deployments in two projects read secrets from. The
# token is write-only: it is never stored in Terraform state.
resource "computesphere_secret_source" "doppler" {
  name      = "doppler-web"
  type      = "doppler"
  auth_type = "service_token"
  config = {
    project = "web"
    config  = "prd"
  }
  credential         = { token = var.doppler_token }
  credential_version = 1 # bump to send a rotated token
  project_ids = [
    "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
    "b2c3d4e5-f6a7-8901-bcde-f12345678901",
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `auth_type` (String) How it signs in: `service_token` (Doppler) or `client_secret` (Azure Key Vault).
- `config` (Map of String) Settings of the type: Doppler `project` and `config`; Azure Key Vault `tenant_id` and `vault`. Changes in place, after a connection test.
- `credential` (Map of String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Sign-in fields of `auth_type`: Doppler `token`; Azure Key Vault `client_id` and `client_secret`. Write-only: it's never stored in Terraform state, and the API never returns it. It's sent on create, and again when `credential_version` or `auth_type` changes. Needs Terraform 1.11 or later.
- `name` (String) Name, unique in the account. Changes in place.
- `type` (String) `doppler` or `azure-kv`. Changing it creates a new secret manager.

### Optional

- `all_projects` (Boolean) Let every project of the account use it, including projects an owner or admin creates later. Can't be set with `project_ids`.
- `credential_version` (Number) Change it to send `credential` again, for example after rotating the token.
- `project_ids` (Set of String) Projects that may use it, each with all its environments. None by default; empty while `all_projects` is true. A project allowed only some of its environments in the console isn't listed here, and the next apply allows all of them again.
- `sync_interval_s` (Number) Seconds between checks for changed secret values.

### Read-Only

- `credential_fingerprint` (String) A fingerprint of the stored credential, to tell whether it changed.
- `id` (String) Secret manager id.
- `ref_count` (Number) How many secrets read from it, in every project.
- `status` (String) `untested`, `ok` or `error`, from the last connection test.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by id. Set credential and credential_version in the configuration:
# the first apply after an import sends the credential once.
terraform import computesphere_secret_source.doppler 9a8b7c6d-5e4f-3a2b-1c0d-ef9876543210
```
